tested_scope.model: 128 finite traces = 4 protocols x 2 stale/current-generation states x 2 clean/ambiguous-response retry states x 2 live/expired request-dedupe states x 2 stable/rebound sink-incarnation states x 2 no-advance/generation-advance-after-precheck states
tested_scope.rate_limit_interruption: Interruption before the sink call is fail-closed with zero effect and cross-invocation checkpoint. Interruption/response loss after a possibly committed sink call is represented by ambiguous-response retry.
tested_scope.effect_identity: stable effect_id; duplicate means the same semantic external effect must not be applied twice
tested_scope.excluded: Byzantine sinks, cryptographic forgery, arbitrary sink APIs lacking the modeled validation primitives, and repository-incarnation safety already falsified in Part128

protocols.sink_local_monotonic_fence: Sink atomically checks a current-generation floor and permanent effect_id ledger, but both are scoped to the current sink incarnation and are lost on sink rebind/reset.
protocols.request_id_only_dedupe: Sink deduplicates request_id only while its dedupe record is live; there is no generation fence.
protocols.repository_precheck_unfenced_sink: Worker checks repository generation immediately before calling a sink that does not itself fence generation or effect_id.
protocols.fail_closed_capability_token: Strong candidate prerequisite: sink atomically validates token(effect_id,generation,sink_incarnation) against its durable current generation/incarnation and permanent effect ledger at apply time; stale incarnation/generation or repeated effect_id is rejected.

sink_local_monotonic_fence.failure_mode: rebind/reset loses the fence/ledger; stale generation, ambiguous retry, or superseded generation can then cross

request_id_only_dedupe.failure_mode: no generation fence plus dedupe expiry/rebind permits stale or duplicate effects

repository_precheck_unfenced_sink.failure_mode: TOCTOU generation advance after precheck and ambiguous-commit retry remain unfenced at the effect boundary

fail_closed_capability_token.scope_condition: Only under the strong modeled prerequisite that sink-side current generation/incarnation and effect ledger are durable and atomically checked at effect application. This prerequisite is not generically available on arbitrary external sinks.

public_precedent.observation: Kafka's broker-side producer epoch is checked against the request epoch and an old epoch can be rejected as InvalidProducerEpoch/producer fencing. This is precedent for putting freshness fencing at the authoritative effect boundary rather than relying only on a client-side precheck.
public_precedent.usage: mechanism analogy only; Kafka is not an accepted dependency for the zero-quota Chat route

observed: The finite model produces 14/32 unsafe traces for sink-local fencing when rebind can erase the fence/ledger.
Repository precheck plus unfenced sink write produces 12/32 unsafe traces.
The strong fail-closed sink capability-token model produces 0/32 unsafe traces under its explicit durability/atomic-validation prerequisite.
observation_vs_inference.inference: Generic external-effect safety needs sink-boundary participation that combines generation/incarnation freshness with permanent effect identity. Client/repository prechecks or expiring request-id dedupe cannot establish the same property. Zero unsafe traces for the capability-token model do not prove generic implementability because its sink-native anti-rollback prerequisite remains unresolved.

phase1_assessment.residual_richer_mode_protected_manual_ex: none in this bounded model/public-doc audit

No hosted runner, Codespaces, cloud compute, external coordinator, paid credit, artifact/LFS/package quota, or user execution is part of the candidate route.

unresolved_children: Prove or falsify a zero-cost Chat-native way for an arbitrary non-repository effect endpoint to preserve or reconstruct a non-rollbackable sink generation/incarnation floor across reset/rebind without introducing external hosted coordination.
Part128 repository-incarnation write-time fencing remains unresolved and is not solved by sink-local effect fencing.
continuation: Part130: execute one bounded sink anti-rollback/bootstrap leaf. Hold Part127 replay semantics, Part128 repository-incarnation blocker, and Part129 external-effect model fixed. Compare (a) sink-native non-rollbackable monotonic epoch, (b) client-carried signed/current certificate with no sink floor, (c) repository-issued capability plus sink-incarnation binding, and (d) fail-closed refusal until a current sink floor is re-established. Include response loss, duplicate retry, stale certificate, sink name reuse, rate-limit interruption, and later retry.
